_note: A battle royale squad's systems, Season 30 where Apex publishes a number (docs/RESEARCH_PHASE_11.md section 6): the bleed-out clock per knock, a revive's 5 s and the 20 health it gives back. The crawl speed, the reach and the launch pad's throw are ours.
_bleedOut: seconds on the floor for the first, second, third and later knocks of a life. It is a trio's clock: the battle royale multiplies it by its squad size's `bleed` (src/config/br.json), so a duo has half of it and a solo has no down at all.
_reviveConfirm: Seconds a reviver waits for the one they revived to say they are up before the revive's credit (its notice, sound and EVO) is given (brplay.ts); no word by then, or word that they are out, and there is none. A state packet takes a tenth of a second; three is for a bad connection.
_crawl: down, you crawl at this fraction of the crouch walk (ours)
_pad: a launch pad on a road: along it and up, m/s (ours; about 33 m along and 6.7 m up)
_ping: how long a ping lasts, s
_evo: EVO as Season 30 counts it (docs/RESEARCH_PHASE_12.md section 2.3): 1 per point of damage you deal (the levels are in items.json), 150 a knock, 100 an assist (you hurt them in the last assistWindow seconds and someone else knocked them; the window is ours), 100 a finisher, a revive 100 for the first two then 25 less each, 100 for looting a care package (once a package). Taking damage earns nothing.
_drop: Landing: the bots drop on the OTHER places while there are any (a squad's own place is theirs), they are spread `apart` metres around a place's drop points so they do not pile onto one, and nobody's gun works for `grace` seconds after they land. Before this you could land beside three bots and be dead before the drop animation finished.
_dive: The skydive, in two states the way Apex flies it: where you look decides the trade between falling and travelling. Look level (flatPitch) and you glide: glideFall m/s down and glideSpeed m/s across, the long way to a far place. Look straight down (downPitch) and you dive: diveFall down and diveSpeed across, the fast way onto the place under you. In between it blends. The drop starts looking 35 degrees down, which lands on about 20 m/s down and 10 across, near the single speed the skydive always had (22 and 9), so a player who never touches the mouse drops as before. botFall is how fast a bot comes down, straight, as it always did. Ours: Apex does not publish its freefall numbers, and its map is ten times the size of this one. mapSeconds is how long the drop keeps the full map over the screen by itself: long enough to see which place you are over and which is next to it, then it steps aside so you can see the ground you are steering onto (M brings it back). It used to stay up for the whole fall, which was fine when looking did nothing.

dive._mapOnBoard: whether boarding the dropship throws the full map up over everything. It used to, and the first thing anyone saw of a match was a map: the ship, the sky, the island and the squad were all behind it. Now the ride is the ride, the minimap and the ship's own line say where it is going, and M opens the map when you want it (src/main.ts boardShip).

_ship: The dropship (src/game/dropship.ts). It flies a straight line across the map at `height` metres and `speed` m/s; the line passes within `pass` metres of the squad's place and comes in from the side that leaves most of the line before it. It is at least minLine metres long (tries angles until one is), so a place near a corner does not get a line that clips the corner in a second. It appears doorsIn seconds short of the edge, so the doors open as it crosses into the map. From 140 m a glide carries about 160 m, so any place within that of the line can be reached, and a dive is on the ground in under 5 s. seat is where a rider's feet are against the ship's middle (inside the hull, which hides them); jumpers leave `exit` metres under it. The camera rides chase metres behind and chaseUp above. A squad follows its jumpmaster (the host) down: each follower is held back metres behind and side metres to one side of the jumpmaster, closing at gain per second, until C breaks it off or the jumpmaster is release metres off the ground. A bot squad leaves the ship as it passes nearest its place, within botJitter seconds of each other squad, each bot botGap seconds after the last. Ours throughout: Apex's ship is a minute's flight over a map ten times this size.
_kdShield: the knockdown shield (Season 28 on): its size is your EVO level's, 200 / 450 / 750; hold fire while down to raise it; it stops what comes from the front (ours: within 70 degrees of where you face); you crawl 45% slower behind it; broken, it stays broken until your next knock
_echoRespawn: A squad mate brought back where they died (ours, after Apex's Deathbox Respawn, Season 29, research 2.1; there are no death boxes now, the owner 2026-10-04): hold interact `time` seconds within `reach` of their echo, the marker that stands where they fell; a green beam and a hum for everyone while it runs; they stand up on it at `health`, the shield back over `shieldRegen` seconds, holding what they died with. In the legacy game each respawn of the same player locks the next out longer (`lockout`, seconds, the last repeating), back to none after `resetAfter` seconds alive; SpeedKills has its own count of restores (speedkills.json life).
_pingWheel: Apex's ping wheel (src/game/brplay.ts PING_INTENTS, src/main.ts): a tap of the ping key marks what you are looking at, and HOLDING it opens a wheel of what the mark MEANS. A squad without voice is legible or it is not, and one mark that says only 'here' is not. The lives are how long each stays up: a plan outlives a warning, because a warning is about this second and a plan is about the next minute.
_colors: Each member of a squad has a colour and a number, the same on every screen in the squad (Phase 27, the owner: "Color code them by blue, green, orange, white ... with a number, like 1 or 3 so its more distinguishable"). The numbers go to the squad's player ids in order (squadview.ts squadSlots), so two screens that know the same ids agree without a word sent. Blue is the teammates' trail blue already (hud.json trails); the orange is kept well off the enemy red (#ff2a3a) of the aim outline and the enemy trails, and the white is a little under full white so the outline drawn in it does not cross the bloom's threshold (render.ts, 0.95) and glow. A squad of more than four goes round the list again.
_mates: How your squad is shown to you (Phase 27, the owner: "his model should always be visible in an outline with a small name above him in the color that he is"). `outline` is the ring round a teammate, through walls: px is its width in screen pixels whatever the distance (the enemy outline's rule, speedkills.json feel.outline), min and max in metres bound it close up and far off. `tag` is the name over them: at any distance, with their shield and health under it within `bars` metres (the plates' 30, hud.json plates) and how far they are from `distFrom` metres, lifted `lift` metres over their feet. `quiet` is how long a teammate may say nothing before their row says the connection is lost: a player standing still sends a keyframe every 2 s (net.json keyframe), up to 5 s apart across the host's relay, and duel.ts drops them at 10. `hurt` is how long a teammate's row flashes after they lose health or shield, and `chip` how long the part they lost stays drawn before the bar drains to it, which is how a squad sees that one of it is in a fight.
